result:
Done.

**Root cause:** `makeMove`'s fifty-move reset at `mkHalf:` compared the moved piece type against `WN` (knight, 2) instead of `WP` (pawn, 1), so pawn moves incremented the clock and knight moves reset it.

**Files touched**
- `variants/bug02/movegen.inc:908` — `cp WN` → `cp WP` (plus two clarifying comments). One byte in the binary: offset 4355, `02`→`01`; length- and cycle-preserving, so no code layout moved.
- `variants/bug02/test_fifty_move.py` — new, 22-case harness regression test.
- `variants/bug02/Makefile` — new `test-fifty` target, invoked at the end of `make test`.
- `FIX_NOTES.md`, `STATE.md` — written at workspace root.
- `variants/bug02/chess.bin` / `chess.tap` — rebuilt in place, so the committed tape is the fixed artefact.

**Gate status**
- Reported symptom gone — PASS. All three repro commands plus the boundary case match the report's "Expected": halfmove 0 after `a2a3` from 98; halfmove 1 and `Your move` after `a2a3,e8e7`; halfmove 41 after `Na1-b3`; `Draw (50-move)` still fires from the 99 position.
- `make test` — PASS (exit 0: golden board, 1.e4 reply, perft, save/load round-trip, 128K banked TT, and the new gate). The wiring was checked to actually fail the build on test failure, not just print.
- New test — PASS. 22/22 on the fixed build; 14 ok / 8 failed on the pre-fix tape, so it would have caught this. Every expected FEN was derived by hand from the chess rules, not recorded from output.
- Characterisation suite — PASS. 57/57, exit 0 (it was 40 ok / 17 failed before the fix, and every one of those 17 differed only in the halfmove field, in the direction pawn-reset semantics predict — the pristine build testifying that it reset on pawns). Baseline not re-recorded; `expected.json` md5-confirmed untouched. Note it needs `--harness ../harness`, as its default path points outside this workspace.
- Review — PASS, closed at round 1 of 3. A fresh reviewer agent, run synchronously, found no defect in the fix; it verified by execution, re-ran `make test` and the characterisation suite itself, and ran extra adversarial probes (both castlings, promotion-capture, under-promotion, black-side draw, search leakage, take-back) — all correct.

Its three non-blocking findings are recorded in `FIX_NOTES.md`. I fixed two anyway since they concerned my own test's soundness: seven cases previously asserted a state indistinguishable from a fresh game, so all cases now assert the whole resulting FEN; and castling coverage was added (16 → 22 cases). Those changes touch the test only — the assembly and tape are byte-identical to what the reviewer verified (md5s match its own measurements), so no further round was required.

**Knowingly left open** — three pre-existing quirks in code this fix does not touch, byte-identical before and after, outside the bug report's scope: a *crafted* halfmove of 255 wraps to 0 on the bare `inc a` (unreachable in real play, since the draw fires at 100 and the game-over loop then accepts only `N`/SPACE); a fired 50-move draw cannot be taken back with `Z`; and a position *loaded* with the clock already ≥ 100 is not declared drawn until the next move.
